messages:
samir: FYI: the latency dashboard's p95 for /v1/respond is oscillating when the routing policy nudges fallback weight. p50 is fine. screenshot: https://dash.redwood/internal/respond_osc.png

claire: saw that in the alert runbook. Is this the same merged-percentile behaviour where a tiny subgroup with huge tail flips the global p95?

samir: Looks like it. Quick query we ran: `SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) FROM rollups WHERE endpoint='/v1/respond'` across 5m windows. After the routing tweak at 2025-05-05T09:03, p95 popped for 7 minutes.

ops-bot: rollout/weight-change service=respond route=slow-fallback old=0.02 new=0.12 user=sam at=2025-05-05T09:03:12Z

metrics-bot: export: overall p95=470ms (n=980), main p95=420ms (n=965), fallback p95=3200ms (n=15)

claire: That's the pattern: fallback n is tiny but tail huge. Two usability problems: (1) Console shows only merged percentile and no signal how much each subgroup contributed; (2) our merge estimator returns a single number with no confidence.

console-team: UX idea: add a micro-pill next to each percentile line with `n=` and a small confidence band (when available). click => "split by tag" dropdown (route_variant, client_region).

samir: Also proposal: introduce a "stability window" indicator on the chart header. It looks at recent sample counts and flags windows where any contributing subgroup had n < 30 during the slice. Visual: amber dot + tooltip "percentile unstable: small subgroup samples".

claire: Backend asks: do we prefer exposing per-tag counts or returning an aggregated `dominant_contributor` label? per-tag counts are more flexible but bigger payloads.

metrics-bot: telemetry-api proposal: `GET /telemetry?endpoint=...&window=5m&include=sample_counts` returns flat arrays: tags[], counts[] (keeps shape shallow). We cap at top 50 tags and include `truncated=true` flag.

console-team: keep it flat arrays only (no nested objects). UI expects shallow lists. Good to cap and show "+x more". Also sanitize tag lengths (<64 chars).

samir: On the estimator side, we can do two things: (A) short-term: compute and return a simple `merge_confidence_pct` using bootstrap heuristics for small n; (B) long-term: store t-digest sketches per shard and return merged t-digest + error bounds.

claire: Another small idea: add a chart mode toggle "de-emphasize small groups" which merges percentiles but downweights groups with n<threshold (configurable, default 10). This would avoid noisy pages while preserving accuracy for large regressions. But we need to be explicit in UI when de-emphasis is applied.

ops-bot: note: add annotation layer for rollout.* and deploy.* events on latency charts. That saved time in past incidents.

metrics-bot: PR checklist: (1) API: sample_counts flat arrays + truncated flag (ENGPLAT-1681), (2) Telemetry: merge_confidence_pct heuristic (ENGPLAT-1682), (3) Console: sample-pill + stability window + de-emphasize toggle (ENGPLAT-1683), (4) t-digest migration spike tests (ENGPLAT-1684).

samir: I'll own the API change and bootstrap confidence calc. Claire, can you drive the pill mockups? Console-team to implement UX.

claire: Yup. I'll mock small-pill variants (compact, with `n=15 · conf=~30%` and tooltip text: "low subgroup samples — percentile may be unstable; try split view").

console-team: Implementation notes: show pill inline, gray-out percentile line when merge_confidence_pct < 50%, add a small caret that opens split-by-tag. Keep payloads shallow.

samir: Operational note for runbooks: when changing routing weights expect transient p95 drift for up to 10 minutes; consult stability dot before paging SRE. I'll add this to the rollout runbook.

claire: Nice. We'll also add a one-line help in the console: "Why did p95 move? Click pill for sample counts and split view."

metrics-bot: scheduled: run t-digest merge accuracy harness on staging with heavy tail shards at=2025-05-05T13:00:00Z owner=metrics-team

samir: Thanks all. Plan: ship sample-pill + stability indicator in next console patch, add API flag to telemetry, then run t-digest validation. Will post PR links here. :thumbsup:
